newsitem.title: USA: Northwestern Steel hurt by shipment drop.
newsitem.headline: Northwestern Steel hurt by shipment drop.

text.p: Northwestern Steel & Wire Co attributed its January 31 second-quarter loss to a decline of more than 15 percent from the prior year in shipments of medium and large structural products, at slightly lower selling prices.

Chairman Robert Gurnitz noted in a statement that semi-finished steel sales declined from first-quarter levels but were substantially higher than in the prior year's second quarter. Average selling prices for small structurals, wire, rod and semi-finished steel products all were below prior year second-quarter levels, Gurnitz said.

In addition to selling price pressures, operating costs were higher in the quarter, the executive said. "A planned outage for the furnace operations and the closure of the Houston plant for 10 days to rebalance the order backlog contributed to poor operating performance," Gurnitz said.

In the medium and heavy structurals segment, "The impending exit of a competitor, relatively low inventories at service centers, improved operating performance in our mills and a positive outlook at the customer level for non-residential construction, should lead to improved results in this important segment of our business," he said.
In the company's stronger markets, rod, wire proeucts and small structurals, price increases have been announced for later in the third quarter, Gurnitz added.

Earlier, Northwestern Steel, a mini-millproducer of structural steel components, reported a second-quarter loss of $0.09 per share compared to a year-ago profit of $0.10 per share. Sales fell to $143.7 million from $149.2 million.
